title: 5 days Upper Lower program review (Week 1)
summary: He reviews week 1 of a viewer's shoulder- and knee-friendly 5-day upper/lower split. He likes the posterior chain and upper back emphasis and gives rep range, exercise order and superset fixes. He also suggests additions for traps, long head triceps and rear delts.
claims: The best programs repeat as an endless cycle; programs that change too much produce artificial PRs without real tonnage progress
Stick with a good hypertrophy program for years instead of jumping every six months; you should progress on its compounds until your prime in your 40s
Fixed 4x8 trap bar deadlifts are fine for static volume, but to push progression use an evolving range like 8-12 or 6-10
Belt squats at 10-12 reps are good; do not go too low, he has seen bad ligament accidents on them
Glute ham raises at 4x15 are excellent; hamstrings have more muscular endurance and tolerate higher reps
Keep reverse hypers and hyperextensions in high rep ranges for injury prevention and hypertrophy; there is no point doing them for 3x3
The belt squat loads the posterior chain while the trap bar deadlift loads the quads more and is not a full hip hinge, whatever EMG data says
Emphasising posterior chain over quads is excellent for knee injury prevention, and the trap bar is easy on the knees
Open the workout with the most strenuous strength compound, not bodyweight pull-ups
Straight barbell overhead press should stay around 4-8 reps for the intensity needed to progress
Supersetting a vertical press with an underhand lat pulldown helps prevent elbow tendonitis
Close grip neutral football bar bench is better at 6-10 than 10-12, and supersetting it with pull-ups as antagonists saves time
Superset cable rows with skull crushers, even on the same bench, to save time
Farmer walks done properly with real weight are like a super deadlift and should not be supersetted
Do bodyweight pull-ups for as many reps as possible rather than a set rep range
Lat pulldowns and cable rows sit well in 8-12; going too heavy turns them into cheat movements using legs and momentum, losing the tension and stretch cables provide
Farmer walks for 1-2 minutes of time are not very conducive to progression
Do skull crushers for 3 sets of 8-12 rather than 2 of 12-15; at 12-15 muscular endurance becomes the limit and the second set drops off
Be careful with neutral-grip curls and pulls, which can overextend the rotator cuff; supinated work is healthy for triceps and shoulder tendons
Box squats are not the best for hypertrophy: people rock back into a good morning and take super wide stances; they are acceptable if posterior chain is the priority
Bodybuilders and recreational lifters should not do supra-maximal box squats or 1RM good mornings as Westside strength athletes do
Hip thrusts are better at 10-15 than 20; they progress fast and should never go to failure, staying fluid and controlled
A 9-12 evolving range works, but the smaller window means weight progression must be adapted
Do not superset strength work like bench, squats, deadlifts, hip hinges, knee flexion or horizontal presses; overhead press paired with a pull is the exception
If shoulder conscious, bench 4 sets of 4-8 with paused reps and no superset; a pause loses no pec tension and is easier on the shoulders
Do not turn T-bar rows into deadlifts; use hamstring and lower back rigidity to hold position and pull with the back; for posterior chain do cheat or Kroc rows instead
A pronated grip on the T-bar row hits less lats and more upper back
Dumbbell overhead press for 3x10-12 is excellent; the hardest part with dumbbells is getting them into position
EZ bar curls work best at 3 sets of 6-10, even 3-7 with strict form, and side raises at 3 sets of 8-12
Include vertical presses; doing only horizontal presses leads to bad shoulders
More pulling than pressing and more posterior chain than quads keeps you healthy long term
Supersetting lifts that hit the same muscle should be a last resort or used deliberately to pre-fatigue
To round out the program add shrugs for traps, behind-the-head cable extensions for the long head, face pulls for rear delts, direct neck work for a bigger neck and wrist flexion for forearms
exercises: loads posterior chain; ligament risk if heavy
posterior chain, not ideal for quads
